pk/math.text: Separates shapes into parts and recombines them to make new shapes or designs
Identifies and describes shapes and their attributes
Uses basic shapes to build, make or represent objects
Builds structures using 3D shapes and shows how pieces fit together to make new shapes
Uses spatial language to describe where things are and how they fit together
Uses complex spatial language related to location, direction and distance
Makes sets up to five objects and answers the “how many” question with the last number counted
Instantly recognizes collections up to five
Counts verbally to at least 10, progressing toward 20
Points and counts 10 - 20 objects accurately
Uses objects, fingers or drawings to count a group and shows the total with the last number counted
Identifies numerals to 10 by name
Explains changes in quantity
Repeats more complex patterns and sequences:
Identifies
Copies
Extends
Creates
Notices and describes patterns seen in natural and designed settings
Uses objects or tools to measure and compare size, weight or capacity, describing results in words or numbers
Describes attributes of measurement using comparative language
Collects simple data independently
Organizes data using charts, graphs or tables with adult support
Interprets data to answer questions with adult support

pk/language.text: Demonstrates more complex receptive language skills:
Understands approximately 4,200 words and expands to at least 10,000 by age of 5
Follows 3-4 step directions
Understands most of what is said at home and school
Understands comparatives (-er) and superlatives (-est)
Follows directions to play a game
Demonstrates knowledge of the rules of conversations:
Speech is understood by strangers 90-100% of the time
Has an expressive vocabulary of more than 2,000 words
Takes turns while speaking and listening
Engages with at least three back and forth exchanges
Produces longer and more complex sentences which are grammatically correct
Can tell a story that stays on topic
Participates in group discussions making comments and asking questions related to the topic
Shows increasing comprehension of a story
Retells familiar stories with key events using some simple sequencing terms:
First
Then
Next
With support, provides basic answers to specific questions about details of a story:
Who
What
When
Where
With support, answers inferential questions about stories and makes predictions or how/why something is happening in a particular moment
Says most sounds correctly when speaking except for a few (l, s, r, v, z, ch, sh, th)
Produces the sound of some known letters
Blends and/or segments word parts or syllables to identify a word, object or picture
Identifies the beginning sounds in words
Identifies words that begin with the same sound
Identifies words that rhyme from a group of 3-4 words
Starts to write in left to right and top to bottom direction
Writes in letter strings, especially using the letters in their own name
Uses invented spelling with:
Beginning sound(s)
Ending sound(s)
Logical sound substitution(s)
Uses a combination of drawing, dictating or emergent writing to convey meaning through writing
Shows an awareness of print:
Locates print on the page
Understands sentences are made of words and words are made of individual letters
Follows print from left to right
Recognizes at least half upper and half lower case letters including letters in own name and letters seen frequently in the environment

pk/science.text: Plans and conducts simple investigations to answer questions or to design solutions to scientific or engineering problems
Uses observational tools to extend the five senses
Observes, investigates and describes objects, materials and other physical science phenomena in the classroom and outdoor environments
Observes, asks questions and begins to recognize patterns and relationships in natural phenomena
Uses observations from investigations to notice similarities and differences in living things and to make guesses about their needs
Describes and compares the properties and motions of objects in terms of speed and direction, based on exploration
Uses prior experiences and/or data from observations to identify patterns in how living and nonliving things stay the same or change over time and/or when conditions change
Analyzes what happened during an investigation to make meaning
Generates explanations and communicates ideas and/or conclusions about investigations:
Communicates with others about questions, actions, ideas, observations or results using labels and adjectives
Draws increasingly complex pictures to represent their observations of objects and/or of changes to objects or the environment
Uses scientific content words when investigating and describing observable phenomena

pk/social.text: Begins to express own thoughts and opinions with confidence while listening to and respecting the thoughts and opinions of others:
Demonstrates preferences and choices
Displays empathy and understanding that others have input and opinions
Begins to identify ways of making choices with others
Demonstrates understanding of an outcome of a discussion
Demonstrates an initial awareness of the concepts of fairness and responsibility toward family and community
Recognize the reasons for rules in the home and early childhood environment and for laws in the community
Identifies features of the environment and people
Recognizes a variety of jobs and how they impact the environment
Describes where something is using detailed vocabulary
Constructs meaning of the world through past events
Explains how past events relate to oneself, family and community
Sequences familiar events by describing events and answering simple questions about time
Engages in extended reciprocal interactions with adults
Accepts guidance, comfort and directions from a range of adults in a variety of environments
Responds to adult requests and directions, may need assistance or prompting
Displays independence and confidence in making choices of wants and needs
Begins to understand how own actions relate to how others perceive them
Imitates social behaviors and shared interests by participating in cooperative and social play
Expresses a broad range of emotions and begins to notice more complex emotions in self
Labels emotions, needs, opinions and desires through preferred communication methods
Demonstrates coping and self-regulation skills to manage a variety of emotions with increasing independence
Shows an increasing ability to understand and accept the connection between their actions and positive or negative consequences
Shows increasing understanding of changing expectations and emotional expression in different settings
Expresses empathy for others and tries to help with an increased range of more complex actions
Sustains positive interactions with one to two preferred peers
Negotiates with others to resolve disagreements with or without prompting from adults:
Engages in sustained periods of cooperative play including strategies to join groups
Identifies friends by names
